risks.title: Authentication system non-functional — any password accepted
risks.description: PKG_SECURITY.authenticate does not verify the password hash. The application has no effective authentication barrier. Combined with cleartext password transmission from the login form, any user with network access can log in as any other user by knowing their email address.
risks.migration_impact: Must be fixed before any cloud or internet-facing deployment.
risks.recommended_action: Implement password hash verification immediately. Enforce TLS/SQL*Net encryption for transport.

risks.title: SSN encryption key exposed in source code
risks.description: Hard-coded AES key for SSN encryption is readable by anyone with access to the PL/SQL package source. All stored SSNs should be considered compromised until the key is rotated and stored securely.
risks.migration_impact: All SSN data must be re-encrypted with a new key stored in Oracle Wallet before migration.
risks.recommended_action: Rotate encryption key immediately; store in Oracle Wallet; re-encrypt all SSN_ENCRYPTED values.

risks.title: SQL injection attack surface in employee search
risks.description: Any authenticated user can inject arbitrary SQL through the employee search form's last name or first name fields, potentially accessing or modifying any data in the HRMS schema.
risks.migration_impact: Must be fixed before exposure to any non-trusted network.
risks.recommended_action: Replace string concatenation with bind variables.

risks.title: Partial payroll commits produce irreconcilable run state
risks.description: A payroll run failure mid-cycle leaves some employees with PAYROLL_DETAILS rows and others without, with no automated detection or repair path. Manual intervention is required to determine which employees were processed.
risks.migration_impact: Payroll data migration must audit for orphaned partial runs.
risks.recommended_action: Add run status tracking per-employee; implement idempotent re-run capability.

risks.title: YTD figures always zero — tax and compliance reporting unreliable
risks.description: All PAYROLL_DETAILS.YTD_AMOUNT fields are hard-coded 0. Any report, W-2 computation, or tax compliance calculation relying on YTD data produces incorrect results.
risks.migration_impact: Historical YTD data in target system must be reconstructed by summing PAYROLL_DETAILS by employee/year.
risks.recommended_action: Fix YTD accumulation before next payroll run.

risks.title: Circular dependency blocks independent module modernization
risks.description: PKG_EMPLOYEE and PKG_PAYROLL cannot be independently deployed, tested, or replaced due to their bidirectional call relationship. Any modernization effort affecting either module must address both simultaneously.
risks.migration_impact: MIGRATION BLOCKER — strangler-fig pattern cannot extract Employee or Payroll independently.
risks.recommended_action: Break cycle before beginning incremental migration.

risks.title: Annual tax law changes require code recompilation
risks.description: US federal tax brackets, SS wage base, and Medicare surcharge thresholds are compile-time literals. Each tax year requires a developer to update source code, recompile, and redeploy. Risk of running stale tax rates.
risks.migration_impact: Tax parameter table must be populated with correct values as part of migration cutover.
risks.recommended_action: Externalize tax parameters to TAX_BRACKETS table; deploy configuration not code for annual updates.

risks.title: PKG_REPORTING.refresh_reporting_tables is a placeholder — reporting data potentially stale
risks.description: The refresh procedure that should keep reporting summary tables current has no implementation. All PKG_REPORTING queries may return stale or incomplete data.
risks.migration_impact: Reporting data migration must account for potentially stale summary tables.
risks.recommended_action: Implement refresh logic or switch PKG_REPORTING to query live tables directly.

risks.title: Time & Attendance import never executes — data gap
risks.description: PKG_INTEGRATION.import_time_attendance file-reading stub with no parsing. Time and attendance data is never imported, meaning any payroll or leave calculations dependent on actual worked hours have no input data.
risks.migration_impact: Integration requirement must be implemented in the target system from scratch.
risks.recommended_action: Implement CSV parsing or replace with API-based integration in target system.

risks.title: Grade-based permissions are coarse — no row-level security
risks.description: PKG_SECURITY.has_permission grants access based on JOB_GRADE only (≥8 full, ≥5 view-all, others leave/employee-view). No row-level security exists. A grade-5 user can see all employee records and compensation data.
risks.migration_impact: Target system must implement proper RBAC with row-level filtering before going live.
risks.recommended_action: Define explicit roles (HR_ADMIN, MANAGER, EMPLOYEE) mapped to fine-grained permissions.

risks.title: Race condition in employee number generation can produce duplicates
risks.description: Under concurrent user activity, two employees may be assigned the same EMP_NUMBER. EMP_NUMBER has a unique index in most normalized designs — if one exists, duplicate inserts would fail at the DB level; if not, duplicate numbers silently corrupt HR records.
risks.migration_impact: Data migration must check for and resolve duplicate EMP_NUMBERs before import.

risks.title: No scheduler job definitions in source — batch schedule unknown
risks.description: DBMS_SCHEDULER jobs for monthly leave accrual, notification queue processing (every 5 min), and potentially payroll batch are referenced in package comments but their definitions are not in the provided source. If jobs are not recreated post-migration, silent data loss occurs.
risks.migration_impact: MIGRATION BLOCKER — scheduler jobs must be documented and recreated in target environment.
risks.recommended_action: Query DBA_SCHEDULER_JOBS in production to capture all job definitions before migration.

risks.title: Direct deposit / ACH disbursement has no implementation — payroll never disbursed to bank accounts
risks.description: EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS is a fully designed split-direct-deposit schema (DEPOSIT_TYPE, PRIORITY_ORDER, PRENOTE_SENT, PRENOTE_DATE) but zero PL/SQL code in the entire source set reads or writes to this table. The payroll lifecycle ends at approve_payroll, which updates PAYROLL_RUNS.STATUS to APPROVED and writes a GL feed file. There is no subsequent step that reads bank account details, generates an ACH NACHA file, calls a bank API, or disburses net pay. The prenote workflow (PRENOTE_SENT='Y' before first deposit) is entirely unimplemented. Employees are paid by an unknown mechanism that is entirely outside this codebase.
risks.source_evidence: schema/tables/02_payroll_tables.sql: EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS full DDL; plsql/packages/PKG_PAYROLL.pkb: no reference to EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS in any procedure
risks.migration_impact: Migration team must locate and document the external disbursement process (manual? third-party? separate batch job?) before any cutover. Target system must implement ACH disbursement from scratch or integrate with a payroll SaaS that provides it.
risks.recommended_action: Investigate production environment for any external batch jobs, NACHA file generators, or manual processes that perform ACH disbursement. Document the full disbursement chain before migration planning is finalised.

risks.title: Bank account encryption scheme undocumented — decryption path unknown
risks.description: ACCOUNT_NUMBER_ENC implies encrypted bank account numbers are stored. No encrypt/decrypt procedures are present in any package in the source. It is unknown whether the same compromised AES key from PKG_SECURITY is used (in which case all bank account numbers are as exposed as SSNs), or whether an entirely separate mechanism exists outside the source set. During data migration, if the decryption mechanism cannot be found, stored bank account numbers may be permanently unrecoverable.
risks.source_evidence: schema/tables/02_payroll_tables.sql: ACCOUNT_NUMBER_ENC VARCHAR2(200) NOT NULL; absence of any decrypt procedure across all 11 package bodies
risks.migration_impact: POTENTIAL DATA LOSS — if decryption key or algorithm cannot be recovered, migrated bank account numbers cannot be decrypted. Must resolve before migration cutover.
risks.recommended_action: Audit PKG_SECURITY source history and DBA-level package grants to find any bank account encryption procedure. Search for Oracle Wallet or DBMS_CRYPTO references outside the provided source set. If not found, plan to re-collect bank account details from employees post-migration.
